dedupe_keys.name: dataset of generative ai workload power profiles nlr kestrel

description: This dataset gives high-resolution power consumption profiles of generative AI jobs run on Kestrel, the high-performance computing system of the US National Laboratory of the Rockies, together with example whole-facility power profiles built with a bottom-up, event-driven data centre energy model. Power was sampled at 5 or 10 Hz on NVIDIA H100 GPU nodes for training, fine-tuning and inference of large language and image generation models, varying datasets and numbers of nodes, and each profile carries metadata on the workload parameters so that studies can be reproduced and compared. It was published in 2026 by Roberto Vercellino, Jared Willard, Gustavo Campos and co-authors at NLR, the laboratory formerly known as NREL, with the paper Measurement of Generative AI Workload Power Profiles for Whole-Facility Data Center Infrastructure Planning (arXiv 2604.07345). Coverage: one supercomputer in Colorado, with synthetic facility-level profiles derived from it. Format and access: standardised power trace files through the DOE OSTI data record with DOI 10.7799/3025227; free of charge, and the associated paper is under CC BY 4.0. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): NLR data catalogue licence (Alliance for Energy Innovation terms: use with attribution and disclaimer). Simulation uses: data centre load models for grid integration and demand response, capacity planning of power and cooling for AI facilities, and resilience studies of grids facing sudden AI load changes. Related records: the York University AI training workload dataset measures single nodes, and the EPRI data centre load projections give regional totals.
